NETWORKs 3/4/5 changed; 1/2/6 proven identical.

header.commentBefore: Supervises the shredder hopper high-level sensor: raises a latched hopper-blockage alarm (and a stop/inhibit demand) when the hopper stays (debounced-)high for a cumulative threshold of time while the plant is running, i.e. the shredder/pusher is not clearing it (S6 request #1, REQ-HBA-001..007). Purely supervisory - it commands no motion and writes no shared tag; the alarm and the stop demand are exposed on its own IO interface and wired to annunciation / the actual stop at a separate integration step (Q-HBA-05). Cumulative timing is pause-and-resume (NEW-HBA-01): losing PlantRunning freezes the elapsed and resumes, so 60 s of blockage need not be contiguous. Built from a plain TON, never TONR (C-406), plus a banked up-accumulator compared against the threshold (see NETWORK 3-4). The alarm latch lives in the RETAIN interface and deliberately survives a power cycle (C-124 carve-out, NEW-HBA-04) - like the sequencer's DischargeConveyorTimeoutFault, a blockage needing a human still needs FaultReset after a restart; all transient timing state is non-retentive and self-clears at startup (NEW-HBA-06, no OB100 edit). Tunables BlockedTimeThreshold (T#60S) and ClearDebounceTime (T#2S) are this instance's own settings (C-307), not shared DB members.

networks.title: Cumulative Blockage-Elapsed Accumulator
networks.beforeText:
NETWORK 3 "Cumulative Blockage-Elapsed Accumulator"
  COMMENT "Banks cumulative high-and-running time across plant-stop pauses (NEW-HBA-01), replacing the former countdown budget (F1/F2/S1 fix, 2026-07-20). AccumulatedElapsed has two provably-disjoint writers, so there is no same-scan race and no next-scan cleanup (the F2/S1 root cause is gone): it is reset to T#0S on a genuine confirmed clear (NOT HighQualified) or on FaultReset, and otherwise banked up by the just-ended segment's elapsed only on a real plant-stop pause (PauseEdge AND HighQualified AND NOT FaultReset - i.e. the hopper is still blocked but the plant stopped). PauseEdge is a constructed falling edge (C-404); it and the bank read PersistenceTimer.ET from before NETWORK 4's TON re-evaluates this scan, so the ET captured is the just-completed segment's, with no separate held-value register needed."
  COIL PauseEdge := NOT BlockActive AND BlockActiveMem
  COIL BlockActiveMem := BlockActive
  MOVE(EN := NOT HighQualified OR IO.FaultReset, IN := ZeroTime) => AccumulatedElapsed
  ADD(EN := PauseEdge AND HighQualified AND NOT IO.FaultReset, IN1 := PersistenceTimer.ET, IN2 := AccumulatedElapsed) => AccumulatedElapsed
networks.afterText:
NETWORK 3 "Cumulative Blockage-Elapsed Accumulator"
  COMMENT "Banks cumulative high-and-running time across plant-stop pauses (NEW-HBA-01). AccumulatedElapsed has two writers that can never fire in the same scan: it goes back to T#0S once the hopper is no longer qualified high (a confirmed clear), and it is otherwise banked up by the just-ended segment's elapsed when the plant stops with the hopper still blocked. An operator FaultReset appears nowhere here: acknowledging an alarm says nothing about the hopper, so it neither discards nor freezes the accumulated evidence (REQ-HBA-005). PauseEdge is the falling edge of BlockActive, taken against the previous-scan copy that the coil below it then updates - the two coils must stay in this order or the edge never fires. Both PauseEdge and the bank read PersistenceTimer.ET before NETWORK 4 re-evaluates the timer this scan, so the elapsed banked is the just-completed segment's, with no separate held-value register needed."
  COIL PauseEdge := NOT BlockActive AND BlockActiveMem
  COIL BlockActiveMem := BlockActive
  MOVE(EN := NOT HighQualified, IN := ZeroTime) => AccumulatedElapsed
  ADD(EN := PauseEdge AND HighQualified, IN1 := PersistenceTimer.ET, IN2 := AccumulatedElapsed) => AccumulatedElapsed

networks.title: Cumulative Persistence Timer
networks.beforeText:
NETWORK 4 "Cumulative Persistence Timer (TON, C-406)"
  COMMENT "Plain TON, never TONR (C-406), times the current contiguous high-and-running segment; FaultReset in its IN forces the current segment back to zero so a reset clears the in-progress time too (F1: reset is history-independent). CumulativeElapsed = AccumulatedElapsed (banked pauses) + this segment's live ET is the total cumulative high-and-running time, compared against BlockedTimeThreshold in NETWORK 5. PT is BlockedTimeThreshold only so a single contiguous segment's ET can itself reach the threshold; the trip is the comparison, not the timer's own Q."
  TON(PersistenceTimer, IN := BlockActive AND NOT IO.FaultReset, PT := IO.BlockedTimeThreshold)
  ADD(EN := TRUE, IN1 := AccumulatedElapsed, IN2 := PersistenceTimer.ET) => CumulativeElapsed
networks.afterText:
NETWORK 4 "Cumulative Persistence Timer"
  COMMENT "Times the current contiguous high-and-running segment, and adds the banked pause time to it: CumulativeElapsed is the total cumulative high-and-running time that NETWORK 5 compares against BlockedTimeThreshold. The timer runs on the blockage-and-running condition alone - an operator FaultReset does not stop, freeze or rewind the segment in progress (REQ-HBA-005). PT is BlockedTimeThreshold only so that a single uninterrupted segment can itself reach the threshold; the trip is the comparison in NETWORK 5, never the timer's own Q."
  TON(PersistenceTimer, IN := BlockActive, PT := IO.BlockedTimeThreshold)
  ADD(EN := TRUE, IN1 := AccumulatedElapsed, IN2 := PersistenceTimer.ET) => CumulativeElapsed

networks.title: Hopper-Blocked Alarm Latch (RETAIN - Survives Power Cycle)
networks.beforeText:
NETWORK 5 "Hopper-Blocked Alarm Latch (RETAIN - Survives Power Cycle)"
  COMMENT "Latched fault (C-123): set when cumulative high-and-running time reaches BlockedTimeThreshold (CumulativeElapsed >= threshold), held until FaultReset. FaultReset gates the whole rung (AND NOT FaultReset) so a reset clears the latch regardless of the trip's current state (F1 fix - the old rung let a still-true trip defeat the reset); paired with NETWORK 3/4 zeroing the accumulator and current segment, a reset requires a fresh full accumulation before re-alarming, identically whether the trip was contiguous or post-pause. Lives in the RETAIN interface and deliberately survives a power cycle (C-124 carve-out, NEW-HBA-04) - a blockage needing a human still needs acknowledgement after a restart, like the sequencer's DischargeConveyorTimeoutFault. Fail-safe: the stop demand below stays asserted until acknowledged."
  COIL IO.HopperBlockedAlarm := (CumulativeElapsed >= IO.BlockedTimeThreshold OR IO.HopperBlockedAlarm) AND NOT IO.FaultReset
networks.afterText:
NETWORK 5 "Hopper-Blocked Alarm Latch (RETAIN - Survives Power Cycle)"
  COMMENT "Latches the hopper-blockage alarm when the cumulative high-and-running time reaches BlockedTimeThreshold, and holds it until an operator acknowledges. The acknowledgement is the moment FaultReset goes true, not the fact that it is true: a reset left on, wired on or stuck on clears the latch once and cannot hold the alarm off afterwards (REQ-HBA-005). Because the reset leaves the accumulated evidence alone, the latch re-evaluates on the very next scan against that same evidence - a hopper still blocked past the threshold re-alarms at once, whether or not the plant is running, while a hopper whose evidence has been discarded stays quiet. The reset pulse is taken against the previous-scan copy that the coil below it then updates - the two coils must stay in this order or the pulse never fires. The latch lives in the RETAIN interface and survives a power cycle: a blockage that needed a human still needs acknowledging after a restart, and the stop demand below stays asserted until it gets one."
  COIL FaultResetEdge := IO.FaultReset AND NOT FaultResetMem
  COIL FaultResetMem := IO.FaultReset
  COIL IO.HopperBlockedAlarm := (CumulativeElapsed >= IO.BlockedTimeThreshold OR IO.HopperBlockedAlarm) AND NOT FaultResetEdge
